title: Iranian delegation lands in Islamabad ahead of ‘make-or-break’ talks
byline: Iran’s negotiating team arrived in Islamabad on Friday for peace talks with the United States, even as Tehran insisted on measures it said needed to be addressed first, throwing last-minute doubt over the meetings.

title: Artemis II astronauts return from moon with splashdown to close out record-breaking lunar voyage
byline: Artemis II’s astronauts returned from the moon with a dramatic splashdown in the Pacific on Friday to close out humanity’s first lunar voyage in more than a half-century.

title: Trump says US will have Strait of Hormuz ‘open fairly soon’
byline: President Donald Trump told reporters on Friday that the U.S. will have the Strait of Hormuz “open fairly soon” but did not elaborate and acknowledged that it will not be an easy step.

title: Artemis II astronauts return from moon with splashdown to close out record-breaking lunar voyage
byline: Artemis II’s astronauts returned from the moon with a dramatic splashdown in the Pacific on Friday to close out humanity’s first lunar voyage in more than a half-century.

title: One dead, 27 injured as bus carrying British tourists crashes in Spain’s La Gomera
byline: At least one person died and 27 were injured after a bus carrying British tourists crashed down a ravine on the Spanish island of La Gomera, emergency services said on Friday.

title: Showers expected in parts of the island after 2pm
byline: Showers or thundershowers will occur at several places in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, North Western, Southern and Uva provinces and in Anuradhapura, Mannar, Kandy and Nuwara-Eliya districts after 2.00 p.m., the Department of Meteorology stated.

title: SJB stages protest near Parliament; minor traffic congestion reported
byline: The Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) staged a protest demonstration along the Parliament access road near Diyatha Uyana in Battaramulla, resulting in minor traffic congestion in the surrounding areas, said Ada Derana reporter.

title: Asia Pacific faces weaker growth and higher inflation from Middle East crisis, ADB warns
byline: Growth in developing Asia and the Pacific is expected to slow this year as the conflict in the Middle East disrupts trade and energy markets, the Asian Development Bank said on Friday, with the extent of the slowdown dependent on how long the crisis persists.

title: Nuwan Thushara apologizes to SLC, expresses willingness to withdraw petition
byline: Sri Lanka cricketer Nuwan Thushara has apologised to Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) regarding his decision to take legal action over the non-issuance of a No Objection Certificate (NOC) to participate in the 2026 Indian Premier League (IPL).

title: Speaker certifies Social Security Contribution Levy (Amendment) Bill
byline: The Speaker of Parliament, Dr. Jagath Wickramaratne, has certified the Social Security Contribution Levy (Amendment) Bill yesterday (09).

title: IRD records over Rs. 600 bln revenue in first quarter of 2026
byline: The Inland Revenue Department (IRD) has reported a strong start to 2026, collecting Rs. 606,002 million in tax revenue during the first quarter of the year, marking a 17.7% increase compared to the same period in 2025.

title: Health authorities urge caution over extreme heat during ‘Avurudu’ festivities
byline: Health authorities have urged the public to exercise caution when organizing New Year (Avurudu) festivals due to the prevailing extreme heat conditions.

title: Michael Jackson biopic ‘spent $15m on reshoots to remove child abuse allegations’ from ending
byline: The upcoming Michael Jackson biopic once promised an “unbiased” look at the King of Pop’s life – until a reported series of costly reshoots completely cut the child abuse allegations against the singer from the film.

title: Melania Trump denies ties to Jeffrey Epstein in rare public statement
byline: US First Lady Melania Trump on April 10 denied that she had any relationship with Jeffrey Epstein and said she was not one of his victims, thrusting the Epstein matter back into the spotlight after her husband had sought to put it behind him.

title: Trump says Iran’s handling of oil through Strait of Hormuz is ‘not the agreement we have’
byline: Iran is doing a very poor job, dishonorable some would say, of allowing Oil to go through the Strait of Hormuz,” Trump wrote on his social media site Thursday evening. “That is not the agreement we have!”

title: School holiday begins; Ministry announces second term schedule
byline: The Ministry of Education (MOE) has announced that the second phase of the first school term for government and government-approved schools concludes today (10).

title: Decision on petitions against post-internship medical appointments on May 8
byline: The Court of Appeal has announced that its order on whether to grant leave to proceed with the petitions challenging the controversial post-internship medical appointment process will be delivered on May 8.

title: Britain celebrates late Queen Elizabeth II as a style icon to mark her centenary
byline: The late Queen Elizabeth II believed the monarch had to be seen to be believed. And she made sure that was true even when Britain’s famously changeable weather intervened, pioneering the use of a clear plastic raincoat so that a stodgy black umbrella didn’t obscure her from public view.

title: More details emerge in private uni. student death at hotel in Homagama
byline: Further details have emerged regarding the death of a student following a clash between two groups of students of a private university in Homagama.

title: Five students of private university arrested over student’s death at hotel in Homagama
byline: Five students of a private university have been arrested by Homagama Police over the death of a 19-year-old students following a clash between students last evening after a New Year (Avurudu) festival.

title: Commissioner General of Motor Traffic further remanded
byline: The Commissioner General of Motor Traffic, Kamal Amarasinghe, who was arrested by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), has been further remanded until April 20 by the Pilessa Magistrate”s Court in Kurunegala.

title: Liquor outlets to remain closed on April 13–14
byline: All liquor outlets across Sri Lanka will remain closed on April 13 and 14, the Excise Department has announced.

title: Warm weather advisory issued for most parts of the country
byline: A warm weather advisory has been issued for tomorrow (11) for residents of the Northern, North-Central, North-Western, Western, Southern and Eastern provinces and in Monaragala District.

title: Showers expected in parts of the island after 2pm
byline: The Department of Meteorology says that showers or thundershowers will occur at several places in Western, Sabaragamuwa, Southern and Uva provinces and in Kandy and Nuwara-Eliya districts after 2.00 p.m.

title: Police arrest 763 in island-wide anti-drug operations
byline: Sri Lanka Police said a total of 28,837 individuals were inspected island-wide yesterday (09) during daily search operations carried out to curb crime and drug-related activities.

title: Artemis II astronauts hurtle home from moon toward splashdown
byline: The four Artemis II astronauts, returning from the world’s first crewed moon voyage in over half a century, hurtled back toward Earth on Friday aboard their gumdrop-shaped Orion spacecraft, headed for a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off Southern California.

title: Special inspections launched island-wide during festive season: PHIs
byline: Special inspection operations have been launched across the island by Public Health Inspectors (PHIs), focusing on public health concerns, within the upcoming festival season, the Public Health Inspectors’ Union of Sri Lanka stated.

title: Russia’s Putin announces Orthodox Easter ceasefire, Ukraine’s Zelenskiy agrees
byline: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday announced a 32-hour ceasefire over a two-day period for Orthodox Easter and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Kyiv would abide by the measure.

title: Global oil prices remain high ahead of UN-Iran talks in Pakistan
byline: The price of global oil remains high ahead of negotiations between the US and Iran in Pakistan this weekend, which will take place amid growing concerns over whether the two-week ceasefire agreement between the countries will hold.

title: GMOA strike continues for second consecutive day
byline: The island-wide strike launched by the Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) in hospitals continues for the second consecutive day today (10).

title: Mahapola scholarship allowance for March credited to students today
byline: The March installment of the Mahapola scholarship allowance, established by the Lalith Athulathmudali Mahapola Higher Education Scholarship Trust Fund, has been credited to university students’ bank accounts today (10).

title: China will not allow fuel crisis to occur in Sri Lanka - Chinese Ambassador
byline: Chinese Ambassador to Sri Lanka Qi Zhenhong has stated that China will not allow a fuel crisis to occur in Sri Lanka under any circumstances.

title: No-confidence motion against Energy Minister defeated in Parliament
byline: The motion of no-confidence submitted by opposition Members of Parliament against Minister of Energy, Kumara Jayakody, was defeated by a majority of 104 votes on Friday (10).

title: Police constable arrested for allegedly accepting liquor bottle as bribe
byline: A Police Constable attached to the Dharmapuram Police Station was arrested yesterday (9) by officers of the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) for allegedly accepting a bottle of liquor as a bribe.

title: Stock of unlabeled cosmetics worth Rs. 10 million seized in Pettah
byline: A stock of unlabeled imported cosmetic products has been taken into custody in Pettah by the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA).

title: Lufthansa flights disrupted as cabin crew stage strike
byline: Lufthansa flights were significantly disrupted on Friday as cabin crew union UFO staged a one-day strike, the airline’s third work stoppage in two months, impacting operations at its Frankfurt and Munich hubs.

title: Hip-hop pioneer, Afrika Bambaataa, dies aged 68
byline: Afrika Bambaataa, one of the founding figures of hip-hop culture, has died at the age of 68, the Hip Hop Alliance has confirmed.

title: Kuwait says National Guard site, vital facilities hit by ‘hostile’ drones
byline: Kuwait said Thursday evening that a National Guard site and several vital facilities were targeted by “hostile” drones.

title: ADB projects Sri Lanka’s economic growth to moderate in 2026
byline: Sri Lanka’s economic growth is projected to moderate from 5.0% in 2025 to 4.0% in 2026, before rising slightly to 4.2% in 2027, according to the Asian Development Bank (ADB).

title: IMF flags coal quality issues driving Sri Lanka power costs
byline: The International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) Mission Chief for Sri Lanka, Evan Papageorgiou, highlighted issues related to coal procurement and its impact on electricity generation costs in the country at a recent press briefing.

title: GMOA to end island-wide strike tomorrow
byline: The Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) has decided to end its island-wide strike action from 8.00 a.m. tomorrow (11).

title: Strict action against individuals who caused damage to Pettah Bus Stand - Dy Minister
byline: Deputy Minister of Transport and Highways Prasanna Gunasena says strict action will be taken against those responsible for causing damages to the newly renovated Pettah Central Bus Stand in Colombo.

title: Two Chinese passengers arrested at BIA over contraband including used iPhones
byline: Two Chinese nationals were arrested by Customs officers at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) for attempting to smuggle a consignment of contraband including used iPhones, suspected to be intended for carrying out computer-related crimes and financial fraud in Sri Lanka.

title: Lebanon says it will take part in talks with Israel if ceasefire in place
byline: A senior official in the Lebanese president’s office has just confirmed to the BBC that Lebanon will participate in direct negotiations with Israel next week if, and only if, there is a ceasefire in place beforehand.

title: Vijay’s unreleased film Jana Nayagan leaked online before TN polls
byline: Tamil superstar Vijay’s final film, Jana Nayagan, has been leaked online, even though it hasn’t been released in theatres yet. On Thursday night, small clips from the film were shared on social media, and by Friday morning, HD prints of the full film were uploaded to piracy sites.

title: Advisory issued for severe lightning
byline: An ‘Amber’ advisory has been issued by the Department of Meteorology for severe lightning in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Southern, Uva provinces, and in Kandy and Nuwara-Eliya districts.

title: Parliament to debate no-confidence motion against Energy Minister today
byline: The no-confidence motion submitted by opposition Members of Parliament against Minister of Energy, Kumara Jayakody, is scheduled to be taken up for debate in Parliament today (10).

title: Former Iranian foreign minister dies of injuries sustained in airstrike – report
byline: Iran’s former Foreign Minister Kamal Kharrazi has died as a result of injuries sustained during a US-Israeli strike earlier this month, according to Iranian media.

title: World Food Programme warns Lebanon facing food security crisis due to Iran war
byline: Lebanon is facing a food security crisis as the Iran war disrupts supplies of goods inside the country, the United Nations World Food Programme said on Friday.

title: Trump says Iran should not charge fees to tankers going through Strait of Hormuz
byline: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday Iran should not charge fees to tankers going through the Strait of Hormuz, which has ‌been blockaded since the start of the Iran war, causing the worst disruption to global energy supplies in history.

title: OpenAI identifies security issue involving third-party tool, says user data was not accessed
byline: OpenAI said on Friday it had identified a security issue involving a third-party developer tool called Axios and is ⁠taking steps to protect the process that certifies its macOS applications are legitimate OpenAI apps.

title: Gap between rich and poor nations is growing even wider, UN report says
byline: The gap between rich and poor nations is growing even wider as actions agreed to by many countries last year, including overhauling the major global financial institutions, remain unfulfilled promises, a U.N. report concludes.

title: GMOA strike ends; Future course of action to be decided
byline: The Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) announced that its 48-hour island-wide token strike ends at 8.00 a.m. this morning (11).

title: Foreign liquor bottles worth over Rs. 20 mln seized in Colombo
byline: The Department of Excise has seized a stock of bottles of foreign liquor worth over Rs. 20 million during a raid carried out targeting several outlets in the Colombo area within the Western Province.

title: Kabir Hashim appointed SJB Chairman
byline: Member of Parliament (MP) of the Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB), Kabir Hashim, has been appointed as the Chairman of the party for the year 2026.

title: Jackson family joins fans in Berlin for premiere of Michael Jackson biopic
byline: Thousands of Michael Jackson fans, many in military jackets or aviator sunglasses inspired by the pop icon’s many famous looks, gathered in Berlin on Friday night for the international premiere of the biopic “Michael” starring the singer’s nephew.

title: 10-year-old schoolgirl killed in bus accident in Mattakkuliya
byline: A 10-year-old schoolgirl was killed after being run over by a bus in the Mattakkuliya area, Ada Derana reporter said.

title: Large crowds arrive at Makumbura MMC for New Year travel
byline: A large number of commuters are reportedly arriving at the Makumbura Multimodal Centre (MMC) since early this morning (11) to travel to their hometowns via the expressways ahead of the Sinhala and Tamil New Year holidays.

title: Secretary to President files complaint seeking CID probe into coal imports since 2009
byline: The Secretary to the President has submitted a complaint to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) this morning (11) requesting a formal investigation into coal imports since 2009, considering the findings of Audit Reports and the findings of Parliament, indicating that irregularities have occurred in the import of coal into Sri Lanka.

title: JD Vance-led US delegation lands in Pakistan for high-stakes ceasefire talks with Iran
byline: A US government aircraft carrying senior officials has landed in Islamabad on Saturday afternoon, setting the stage for crucial negotiations with Iran aimed at ending a six-week war that has shaken the Middle East and global economy, Reuters reported.

title: Iran’s new supreme leader has severe and disfiguring wounds – report
byline: Iran’s new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is still recovering from severe facial and leg injuries suffered in the airstrike that killed his father at the beginning of the war, three people close to his inner circle told Reuters.

title: EU airline industry warns of fuel shortages if Strait of Hormuz stays closed
byline: Europe will suffer jet fuel shortages in just three weeks if the the Strait of Hormuz does not reopen, the trade body for the continent’s airports has warned.

title: QR code not necessary for petrol-powered vehicles until April 18 - CPC
byline: The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) says that owners of petrol-powered vehicles can obtain fuel without the QR code-based fuel quota system from midnight today (11) until April 18, 2026.

title: Sri Lanka welcomes ceasefire in West Asia, urges durable solution
byline: Sri Lanka today said it welcomes the announcement of a temporary ceasefire in West Asia and the forthcoming dialogue.

title: Chinese national arrested with cigarettes worth nearly Rs. 4 mln at BIA
byline: A Chinese national has been arrested at Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) in Katunayake for attempting to smuggle a consignment of Chinese-manufactured cigarettes worth nearly Rs. 4 million into the country.

title: No fertilizer shortage: Govt. confirms surplus stocks
byline: Farmers should not develop unnecessary fear regarding the current fertilizer situation in the country, the Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Livestock, Namal Karunaratne stated.

title: No petrol shortage until June end, diesel supplies sufficient until May end: CPC Chairman
byline: A total of 12 refined fuel shipments are scheduled to arrive in April, the Chairman of the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC), D.J. Rajakaruna confirmed.

title: Public urged to send videos related to reckless driving to police via WhatsApp
byline: The Police Headquarters has introduced a dedicated WhatsApp number 070-4755600 for the general public to submit videos related to reckless and dangerous driving incidents.

title: Maldivian President to visit Sri Lanka next month
byline: The President of the Maldives, Mohamed Muizzu is scheduled to visit Sri Lanka next month.

title: US Vice President JD Vance meets Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif
byline: US Vice President JD Vance has met with Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

title: US intelligence indicates China preparing weapons shipment to Iran, CNN reports
byline: US intelligence indicates China is preparing to deliver new air defense systems to Iran within the next few weeks, CNN ⁠reported late on Friday, citing three people familiar with recent intelligence assessments.

title: Advisory issued for severe lightning
byline: An ‘Amber’ advisory has been issued by the Department of Meteorology for severe lightning in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Southern, Uva provinces and in Kandy and Nuwara-Eliya districts.

title: Iran unable to fully reopen Hormuz as it lost track of mines planted: US officials
byline: Iran is unable to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz for shipping due to its self-inflicted problem: It cannot locate all the mines it laid in the waterway to block the passage amid war, the New York Times reported, citing US officials.

title: US agrees to release frozen Iranian assets in Qatar, other banks: Report
byline: A senior Iranian source  said on Saturday the U.S. had agreed to release Iranian frozen assets that were held in Qatar and other foreign banks, welcoming ⁠the move as a sign of “seriousness” in reaching a deal with Washington in talks in Islamabad.

title: Passenger arrested at BIA for smuggling ornamental plants
byline: A Sri Lankan passenger was arrested by Customs officers at Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) in Katunayake in the early hours today (11) for attempting to smuggle packages of ornamental plants into the country.

title: Sri Lanka’s workers’ remittances exceed USD 2.2 bln in first three months of 2026
byline: Sri Lanka received USD 814.8 million in workers’ remittances in March 2026, according to the latest figures released by the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL).
